contacto.sobre-el-guia-y-el.t: About the guide and the service

contacto.estoy-en-formacion-oficial-como.t: I'm in official training as a Wanderleiter — a certified hiking guide according to Swiss standards. I can already operate legally as a guide on tours up to T3 in summer and WT2 in winter. I say this transparently because I believe honesty is the basis of trust.

contacto.que-pasa-si-hay-mal.t: What happens if the weather is bad on the day of the hike?

contacto.la-seguridad-manda-siempre-si.t: Safety always comes first. If the weather poses a real risk, I cancel the activity without hesitation. In that case you can choose between rescheduling at no extra cost or a full refund. If the weather is grey but safe, we go — the mountains are beautiful with clouds too.

contacto.cuantas-personas-van-en-cada.t: How many people are on each departure?

contacto.maximo-10-personas-por-salida.t: Maximum 10 people per departure. I'm not a mass-tour operator — I prefer groups where I can get to know each person and adapt the pace to the real group, not to a statistical average.

contacto.puedo-reservar-una-salida-priva.t: Can I book a private departure just for my group?

contacto.si-totalmente-si-sois-un.t: Yes, absolutely. If you're a group of friends, family or colleagues, you can book the departure exclusively for yourselves. Write to me and we'll organise the details.

contacto.necesito-un-seguro-especial-par.t: Do I need special insurance to take part?

contacto.recomiendo-encarecidamente-tene.t: I strongly recommend having personal accident insurance and, if possible, a Rega card (Swiss Air Rescue). A mountain rescue can cost between CHF 1,000 and CHF 10,000. It's not mandatory to take part, but it would be irresponsible of me not to warn you.

contacto.que-pasa-si-alguien-del.t: What happens if someone in the group is injured on the trail?

contacto.tengo-formacion-en-primeros-aux.t: I have mountain first-aid training and always carry a full first-aid kit. In case of injury, we give first aid, assess the severity and contact the emergency services if necessary. Nobody is ever left alone in the mountains.

contacto.no-tengo-experiencia-en-senderi.t: I have no hiking experience. Can I take part?

contacto.depende-de-la-ruta-el.t: It depends on the tour. The Creux du Van (T2) is perfect for beginners with basic good fitness. The other two tours (T3) require a bit more experience and fitness. Tell me about your situation and I'll honestly tell you which tour is right for you.

contacto.que-significa-t2-y-t3.t: What do T2 and T3 mean?

contacto.son-los-niveles-de-dificultad.t: They are the difficulty grades of the Swiss Alpine Club (SAC). T1 is a stroll on flat paths. T2 is hiking with elevation gain and uneven but well-marked terrain. T3 adds exposed terrain and trails that aren't always visible. WT2 is the winter equivalent with snow.

contacto.se-puede-hacer-el-creux.t: Can the Creux du Van be done in winter?

contacto.si-con-las-condiciones-adecuada.t: Yes, under the right conditions. In winter the landscape is completely different — and spectacular. With a lot of snow, hiking crampons may be needed. Check availability and conditions before booking. More details in the Creux du Van guide.

contacto.depende-de-la-edad-condicion.t: It depends on age, fitness and the tour. Under-18s must always be accompanied by an adult. For T3 tours I don't recommend children under 12–14. Tell me the specific case and we'll assess it together.

contacto.que-incluye-exactamente-el-prec.t: What exactly does the price include?

contacto.el-precio-incluye-la-guia.t: The price includes the full guide in Spanish throughout the activity. Kandersteg 2 days also includes a night in the hut, dinner and breakfast. Not included: transport to the starting point and personal insurance.

contacto.como-llego-al-punto-de.t: How do I get to the starting point?

contacto.todas-las-rutas-son-accesibles.t: All tours are accessible by Swiss public transport (SBB/CFF). When I confirm the booking I send you detailed instructions — train, PostBus, meeting time and exact point.

contacto.puedo-cancelar-si-cambio-de.t: Can I cancel if my plans change?

contacto.si-con-mas-de-14.t: Yes. More than 14 days in advance, full refund. Between 7 and 14 days, 75%. Between 3 and 6 days, 50%. Less than 48 hours, no refund. See the full policy in the T&C.

contacto.clas-tours-opera-desde-ipsach.t: Clas Tours operates from Ipsach, in the Canton of Bern — in the heart of Switzerland, a few minutes from Lake Biel and with direct access to the main tours of the Bernese Oberland and the Jura.

nosotros.colombiano-viviendo-en-los-alpe.t: A Colombian living in the Swiss Alps. Hiking guide in training. And the person who will accompany you on your next mountain adventure — in Spanish, at your pace, with safety first.

nosotros.santiago-guia-de-clas-tours.t: Santiago, Clas Tours guide, smiling in a yellow jacket in the mountains

nosotros.llegue-a-suiza-hace-anos.t: I came to Switzerland years ago with a backpack and a strong desire to understand this country. I soon discovered that the Alps aren't just a pretty landscape you see from the train — they're something you feel when you walk on them, when you breathe that air, when you reach a ridge and the whole world opens up before you.

nosotros.pero-tambien-descubri-algo-que.t: But I also discovered something that bothered me: for the Spanish-speaking community, that experience was almost out of reach. Not for lack of desire, but because of barriers — the language, not knowing where to start, not having someone you trust to explain how the mountains work here.

nosotros.clas-tours-nacio-para-cambiar.t: Clas Tours was born to change that. So that any Spanish speaker — living in Switzerland or visiting — can experience the Swiss mountains with total confidence, understanding every instruction, every risk, every wonder along the way.

nosotros.actualmente-estoy-en-formacion-.t: I am currently training as a Wanderleiter — a certified hiking guide according to Swiss standards — because if you're going to guide people in the mountains, you have to do it right or not at all.

nosotros.santiago-de-pie-en-un.t: Santiago standing at a viewpoint above a turquoise lake, with hiking poles

nosotros.en-la-montana-no-hay.t: In the mountains there are no second chances. I'd rather shorten a route or turn back than put anyone at risk. The group's safety always comes first, without exception.

nosotros.si-una-ruta-no-es.t: If a tour isn't for you, I'll tell you. If conditions aren't right, I cancel. I don't sell experiences I can't guarantee. I'd rather have a disappointed client today than an injured one tomorrow.

nosotros.no-soy-un-guia-de.t: I'm not a mass-tour guide. Maximum 10 people. I know every participant's name, adapt the pace, answer questions. You're not a number on a list — you're the reason for the departure.

nosotros.no-hago-esto-por-cumplir.t: I don't do this to tick a box. The Alps still thrill me after walking them many times. That energy is contagious — and it's what turns a hike into a lifelong memory.

nosotros.la-montana-no-es-un.t: The mountain isn't an amusement park. We leave no trace, respect fauna and flora, and follow the Swiss hiking code. If we don't look after the mountains, there will be no mountains to guide.

nosotros.no-es-solo-que-hablo.t: It's not just that I speak Spanish — I think in Spanish, understand fears in Spanish, celebrate summits in Spanish. There's a huge difference between a guide who translates and one who really talks to you.

nosotros.la-montana-exige-preparacion-re.t: The mountains demand real preparation. This isn't a hobby I turned into a business — it's a vocation I'm building with official training, real tours and a lot of respect for the mountains.

nosotros.formacion-oficial-suiza-para-gu.t: Official Swiss training for hiking guides. Covers navigation, meteorology, mountain first aid, group technique and risk management.

nosotros.senderismo-de-montana-hasta-cla.t: Mountain hiking up to T3 on the SAC scale (Swiss Alpine Club). Exposed terrain, trails not always marked.

nosotros.senderismo-de-invierno-hasta-cl.t: Winter hiking up to WT2 on the SAC scale. Snow tours on terrain of low technical difficulty.

nosotros.formacion-en-primeros-auxilios-.t: First-aid training applied to mountain environments: emergency management, communication with rescue services, stabilising injured people on the trail.

nosotros.aqui-van-fotos-reales-de.t: Here are real photos from the departures — the landscapes, the groups, the moments that make it all worthwhile.

guia.creux-du-van.el-creux-du-van-es.t: The Creux du Van is a natural amphitheatre in the canton of Neuchâtel, often called the "Swiss Grand Canyon". It is about 1,400 metres wide with walls more than 150 metres high. It is a nature reserve, and on its ledges lives a colony of ibex (alpine wild goats) that was reintroduced in the 1960s.

guia.creux-du-van.es-una-de-las-caminata.t: It is one of the most spectacular day hikes in the Jura, and it is easy to reach by public transport.

guia.creux-du-van.la-caminata-clasica-sa.t: The classic hike starts at Noiraigue station, at about 725 m altitude. There are hourly trains from Neuchâtel and the journey takes around 20 minutes. If you are coming from Biel/Bienne, the route goes via Neuchâtel. Always check the up-to-date timetables at SBB, and confirm the last train back before setting off.

guia.creux-du-van.hay-parqueaderos-ofici.t: There are official car parks, and parking outside them is prohibited within the reserve (camping is not allowed either):

guia.creux-du-van.de-mayo-a-octubre-por.t: May to October, from the north: Couvet (Soliat), about a 5-minute walk from the edge, and Noiraigue (Ferme Robert), at the foot of the cirque.

guia.creux-du-van.de-mayo-a-octubre-por-.t: May to October, from the south: Provence (Soliat), about 5 minutes from the edge, and Gorgier or Bevaix (Grand'Vy), about 15 minutes.

guia.creux-du-van.de-noviembre-a-abril-l.t: November to April: the Couvet and Provence car parks are about a 40-minute walk from the Creux. The road between Provence and Couvet is not salted and requires winter tyres or chains.

guia.creux-du-van.fuente-tourisme-neucha.t: Source: Tourisme neuchâtelois, access and parking. Check conditions there before you go.

guia.creux-du-van.la-ruta-circular-desde.t: The circular route from Noiraigue, step by step

guia.creux-du-van.es-el-recorrido-mas-co.t: It is the most complete route and the easiest to organise by public transport. It is well signposted.

guia.creux-du-van.estacion-de-noiraigue-.t: Noiraigue station. You leave along Rue des Tilleuls, cross the railway line and the River Areuse.

guia.creux-du-van.hasta-les-illons-camin.t: To Les Œillons. Gradual uphill path through the forest.≈ 50 min

guia.creux-du-van.sentier-des-14-contour.t: Sentier des 14 Contours. Fourteen bends up to Le Soliat, with yellow markings.≈ 1 h 30

guia.creux-du-van.el-borde-del-circo-cam.t: The edge of the cirque. You walk along the ridge with views into the void and, on clear days, towards the Alps. Look at the ledges and the forest: this is where ibex are most often seen. This is where it is worth spending the most time on photos and a break.

guia.creux-du-van.bajada-a-la-ferme-robe.t: Descent to Ferme Robert. Descent via the Fontaine Froide to the farm, at about 970 m.≈ 1 h 30

guia.creux-du-van.tiempos-de-referencia-.t: Reference times for continuous walking. With breaks, lunch and photos, allow 4 to 6 hours in total.

guia.creux-du-van.borde-del-anfiteatro-d.t: Edge of the Creux du Van amphitheatre with the rock wall and forest

guia.creux-du-van.vista-del-creux-du-van.t: View of the Creux du Van from the trail, with clouds over the Jura

guia.creux-du-van.paredes-de-roca-del-cr.t: Rock walls of the Creux du Van from above

guia.creux-du-van.ibices-en-el-bosque-ce.t: Ibex in the forest near the Creux du Van

guia.creux-du-van.el-borde-no-tiene-bara.t: The edge has no railings. The outer trail, marked white-red-white, runs along the wall with no protection at all. It is not for anyone with a fear of heights, and demands care with children and dogs.

guia.creux-du-van.manten-distancia-del-b.t: Keep your distance from the edge, especially in wind, fog or wet ground. A photo isn't worth the risk.

guia.creux-du-van.hay-una-variante-mas-e.t: There is a steeper variant, the Sentier du Single, which gets slippery with wet leaves and damp rock.

guia.creux-du-van.a-1-400-m-puede.t: At 1,400 m it can be very cold, even close to 0 °C in the cold months. Bring a warm layer even if the weather is nice down below.

guia.creux-du-van.a-finales-de-octubre-o.t: At the end of October it gets dark around 6pm. Plan an early start and check the last train.

guia.creux-du-van.consulta-el-pronostico.t: Check the forecast before setting off on MeteoSwiss.

guia.creux-du-van.los-perros-deben-ir-co.t: Dogs must be on a lead.

guia.creux-du-van.con-los-ibices-manten-.t: With the ibex, keep your distance: don't feed them, chase them or disturb them, even if they approach the trail.

guia.creux-du-van.no-se-pueden-hacer-fue.t: No fires (except in authorised places) or camping.

guia.creux-du-van.no-se-pueden-recoger-p.t: Do not pick plants, flowers or mushrooms, or disturb the animals.

guia.creux-du-van.basado-en-el-reglament.t: Based on the regulations of the Neuchâtel nature reserves. Rules can change, so check the official information before you go.

guia.creux-du-van.otono-la-mejor-epoca-p.t: Autumn: the best time for many. The air is clearer, views reach as far as the Alps and there are fewer people. Ibex are often seen on the ledges below the edge.

guia.creux-du-van.verano-el-sendero-esta.t: Summer: the trail is in its best condition, but it is when there are the most visitors. Better on weekdays or early.

guia.creux-du-van.invierno-se-puede-pero.t: Winter: it can be done, but under different conditions. With snow you need hiking crampons, and paths can be dangerous.

guia.creux-du-van.calzado-de-senderismo-.t: Hiking footwear with a good sole (mandatory).

guia.creux-du-van.ropa-por-capas-y-una.t: Layered clothing and a jacket, plus a warm layer for the edge.

guia.creux-du-van.agua-y-algo-de-comer.t: Water and something to eat. There is a restaurant at Le Soliat, but don't count on it without confirming it is open.

guia.creux-du-van.bastones-recomendados-.t: Poles (recommended in winter) and hiking crampons if there is snow.

guia.creux-du-van.gorra-protector-solar-.t: Cap, sunscreen and a headlamp if you'll be out late.

guia.creux-du-van.cuanto-se-tarda-en-cam.t: How long does it take to hike the Creux du Van?

guia.creux-du-van.el-circuito-clasico-de.t: The classic circuit from Noiraigue is about 12 km and takes 4 to 6 hours, depending on pace and breaks.

guia.creux-du-van.se-puede-llegar-en-tra.t: Can you get there by public transport?

guia.creux-du-van.si-hay-trenes-a-noirai.t: Yes. There are trains to Noiraigue from Neuchâtel, and the walking route starts from there. Confirm the timetables, especially the last train back.

guia.creux-du-van.se-puede-hacer-en-invi.t: Can it be done in winter?

guia.creux-du-van.si-con-las-condiciones.t: Yes, in the right conditions and with equipment (hiking crampons if there is snow). Paths can be dangerous, so check conditions before you go.

guia.creux-du-van.se-ven-ibices-en-el.t: Do you see ibex at the Creux du Van?

guia.creux-du-van.con-frecuencia-si-en-l.t: Often, yes. The reserve is home to a colony of ibex (alpine wild goats) reintroduced in the 1960s, and they are seen on the ledges below the edge and sometimes on the trail itself. In autumn they tend to be easier to spot. Watch from a distance and without disturbing them.

guia.creux-du-van.se-puede-ir-con-perro.t: Can you go with a dog?

guia.creux-du-van.si-pero-siempre-con-co.t: Yes, but always on a lead, and with great care: the edge of the cirque has no railings.

guia.creux-du-van.es-apto-para-quien-tie.t: Is it suitable for people with a fear of heights or with children?

guia.creux-du-van.la-ruta-en-si-es.t: The route itself is of moderate difficulty, but the edge is unprotected. Anyone with a fear of heights should avoid the outer trail, and with children you need to hold their hand near the edge.

guia.creux-du-van.no-necesitas-experienc.t: You don't need technical experience, but you do need basic fitness: it's about 800 metres of cumulative ascent in a day.

guia.creux-du-van.creux-du-van-con-clas.t: Creux du Van with Clas Tours

guia.kandersteg-bluemlisalphutte.kanders.t: Kandersteg in 2 days: from Griesalp to the Blüemlisalphütte and the Oeschinensee

guia.kandersteg-bluemlisalphutte.subes-p.t: You climb through the Griesalp valley, sleep at 2,840 m in a Swiss Alpine Club hut, watch the sunrise over the Alps and descend to the blue Oeschinensee, with an optional swim. This is what you need to know.

guia.kandersteg-bluemlisalphutte.grupo-d.t: Group of hikers climbing the rocky trail towards the Hohtürli, with the Bernese valleys and a lake in the background

guia.kandersteg-bluemlisalphutte.es-una-.t: It is one of the most complete mountain tours in the Bernese Oberland: you cross from the Kiental valley to Kandersteg via the Hohtürli pass (2,778 m) and sleep at the Blüemlisalphütte (2,840 m), at the foot of the Blüemlisalp massif. The next day you descend to the Oeschinensee, one of the most photographed lakes in Switzerland, and from there to Kandersteg.

guia.kandersteg-bluemlisalphutte.hecha-e.t: Done over two days it's a different experience from doing it in one go: you reach the hut with time to spare, have dinner with a view and watch the sunset and sunrise in the high mountains.

guia.kandersteg-bluemlisalphutte.datos-d.t: Data from Bergwelten (Griesalp – Hohtürli – Kandersteg: 16.1 km, 7 h 45 min in total, T3). The SAC rates the ascent from Griesalp to the hut as T2 (4 h, 1,450 m); BLS and Bergwelten rate it T3. Sources at the bottom of the page.

guia.kandersteg-bluemlisalphutte.el-nomb.t: The name means something like "alp of the little flowers". The Blüemlisalp is a glaciated massif with peaks over 3,600 m: the Blüemlisalphorn (3,660 m) is the highest, next to the Wyssi Frau (3,648 m) and the Morgenhorn (3,620 m). Folk tradition tells that there was once a very rich alp whose inhabitants, out of pride, were buried under the ice. It is a legend, but it helps to imagine why this wall of ice above green meadows is so impressive.

guia.kandersteg-bluemlisalphutte.el-blue.t: The Blüemlisalphorn was first climbed on 27 August 1860: Leslie Stephen, R. Liveing and J. K. Stone, with guides Melchior Anderegg and Pierre Simond. They left the Oeschinen chalets at 2am and reached the summit around 8. That is why the massif is known as one of the cradles of mountaineering.

guia.kandersteg-bluemlisalphutte.la-blue.t: The Blüemlisalphütte belongs to the Blüemlisalp section of the Swiss Alpine Club (SAC), at 2,840 m, very close to the Hohtürli. It is the starting point for many ascents in the area, and a few minutes away there is a climbing area. It has more than a hundred places and is part of the multi-day route called the Bärentrek.

guia.kandersteg-bluemlisalphutte.la-plac.t: The plaque on the façade says it: the building was built in 1946–1947 and extended in 1988/89. In summer 2023 there was construction work, and the hut stayed open to guests.

guia.kandersteg-bluemlisalphutte.placa-e.t: Plaque on the façade of the Blümlisalphütte: height 2840 m, property of the SAC Blümlisalp section, built 1946-1947, extension 1988/89

guia.kandersteg-bluemlisalphutte.el-oesc.t: The Oeschinensee lies at 1,578 m, covers a little over 1 km² and is about 56 m deep. It was formed by ancient rockslides that dammed the valley. In the 17th and 18th centuries sulphur was mined on the Oeschinenalp, and since 2007 the lake has been part of the UNESCO World Heritage Site Swiss Alps Jungfrau-Aletsch.

guia.kandersteg-bluemlisalphutte.tren-ha.t: Train to Reichenbach im Kandertal (hourly RegioExpress from Bern or Brig) and from there PostBus 220 to Griesalp. BLS describes it as the steepest bus route in Europe: very tight hairpin bends, so take it calmly. In 2026 it ran from 23 May to 18 October. Confirm the timetables each season at BLS and SBB.

guia.kandersteg-bluemlisalphutte.hay-par.t: There are pay car parks at Tschingelsee and at Griesalp. Keep in mind that you finish in Kandersteg, not where you left the car, so plan your return: the most practical way is to arrive by public transport.

guia.kandersteg-bluemlisalphutte.el-fina.t: The finish is in Kandersteg, which has a train station. From the gondola valley station there is a bus to the station. If you are going down by the Oeschinensee gondola, in 2026 it ran from 8:30 to 18:00 (until 20 September) and until 17:00 (21 September to 8 November); the downhill ticket cost CHF 26.20 for adults and CHF 14.10 with a Half Fare card or for children. Check times and prices before you go.

guia.kandersteg-bluemlisalphutte.fuentes.t: Sources: BLS, Hohtürli-Passwanderung and Oeschinensee, gondola.

guia.kandersteg-bluemlisalphutte.dia-1-d.t: Day 1: from Griesalp to the Blüemlisalphütte

guia.kandersteg-bluemlisalphutte.subida-.t: Ascent of about 4 to 4 h 30 of actual walking, with +1,450 m of elevation gain. With breaks, allow 5 to 6 hours.

guia.kandersteg-bluemlisalphutte.griesal.t: Griesalp (1,408 m). You set off on a marked path through forest and meadows.

guia.kandersteg-bluemlisalphutte.underi-.t: Underi and Oberi Bundalp (1,840 m). Grazing alps, the last gentle stretch before the steep climb.

guia.kandersteg-bluemlisalphutte.la-cues.t: The Hohtürli climb. A steep rocky path with chain-secured sections leads up to Uf der Wart (2,508 m).

guia.kandersteg-bluemlisalphutte.valle-r.t: Rocky valley to the Hohtürli (2,778 m). Stone landscape, close to the Blüemlisalp glacier. Here you enter the pass linking Kiental with Kandersteg.

guia.kandersteg-bluemlisalphutte.la-blue.t: The Blüemlisalphütte (2,840 m). A few minutes above the pass. You arrive, settle in, and there is time to rest, have dinner and watch the sunset.

guia.kandersteg-bluemlisalphutte.atardec.t: Sunset at the Blüemlisalphütte, with the stone hut and people on the terrace

guia.kandersteg-bluemlisalphutte.amanece.t: Sunrise from the hut, with a stone shed and the Bernese valleys in the background

guia.kandersteg-bluemlisalphutte.se-duer.t: You sleep in shared dormitories (bunks). The hut provides blankets, but you must bring a sleeping-bag liner.

guia.kandersteg-bluemlisalphutte.incluye.t: Dinner and breakfast (half board) are included. The cooking is homemade, with wines mostly from the Valais. There is a vegetarian menu if requested in advance.

guia.kandersteg-bluemlisalphutte.se-acep.t: Card and cash are accepted for drinks.

guia.kandersteg-bluemlisalphutte.la-temp.t: The staffed season runs from mid-June to mid or late October, and is in full operation from July to September.

guia.kandersteg-bluemlisalphutte.dia-2-d.t: Day 2: from the hut to the Oeschinensee and Kandersteg

guia.kandersteg-bluemlisalphutte.bajada-.t: Descent of about 1,680 m. Allow about 3 to 4 h of walking to Kandersteg, without breaks and without a swim (7 h 45 min total route minus the first day's ascent).

guia.kandersteg-bluemlisalphutte.desayun.t: Breakfast and departure. You set off early to have more time at the lake. The descent heads west.

guia.kandersteg-bluemlisalphutte.oberbar.t: Oberbärgli (1,978 m). Then comes a steep descent to Underbärgli, so it's wise to take it calmly and with poles.

guia.kandersteg-bluemlisalphutte.underba.t: Underbärgli (1,800 m). There are restaurants, a good spot for a break.

guia.kandersteg-bluemlisalphutte.oeschin.t: Oeschinensee (1,578 m). Long stop: photos, lunch and, if the weather allows, a swim.

guia.kandersteg-bluemlisalphutte.hasta-k.t: To Kandersteg. On foot along the Oeschibach stream, or by gondola for the last ~400 m of descent.

guia.kandersteg-bluemlisalphutte.el-lago.t: The turquoise Lake Oeschinensee with the walls and glaciers of the Blüemlisalp in the background

guia.kandersteg-bluemlisalphutte.el-oesc.t: The Oeschinensee and the Blüemlisalp walls

guia.kandersteg-bluemlisalphutte.vista-d.t: View of the Oeschinensee from above, with fresh snow on the peaks

guia.kandersteg-bluemlisalphutte.el-lago.t: The lake with snow in autumn

guia.kandersteg-bluemlisalphutte.valle-d.t: The Kandersteg valley seen during the descent from the Hohtürli

guia.kandersteg-bluemlisalphutte.tiempos.t: Reference times for continuous walking. Route source: Bergwelten, Hohtürli and Blüemlisalphütte.

guia.kandersteg-bluemlisalphutte.banarse.t: Swimming in the Oeschinensee: yes or no?

guia.kandersteg-bluemlisalphutte.si-se-p.t: Yes, you can: swimming is allowed, at each person's own risk. There are no changing rooms, showers or lifeguards. The shallow south and west shores are the most used for cooling off.

guia.kandersteg-bluemlisalphutte.el-agua.t: The water is cold. It's a mountain lake at 1,578 m. One reference reading showed about 11 °C; in high summer it can rise, but expect cold.

guia.kandersteg-bluemlisalphutte.entra-d.t: Go in slowly, don't jump in all at once, and stay close to the shore.

guia.kandersteg-bluemlisalphutte.despues.t: After a long descent and with a warm body, a short dip is the most sensible thing. Dry off and warm up quickly.

guia.kandersteg-bluemlisalphutte.lleva-t.t: Bring swimwear and a small towel; they take up little space.

guia.kandersteg-bluemlisalphutte.no-es-u.t: It is not an easy hike. It has a long, steep ascent, a chain-secured section towards the Hohtürli and a steep descent. It requires good fitness, mountain footwear and no fear of heights.

guia.kandersteg-bluemlisalphutte.nieve-a.t: Snow early in the season. In June and sometimes in October there may be snowfields on the Hohtürli. Check the state of the path with the hut or with Kandersteg before setting out.

guia.kandersteg-bluemlisalphutte.caida-d.t: Rockfall at the Oeschinensee. Because of the risk of rockfalls (partly linked to thawing permafrost) there were trail and shore closures in 2020, 2021 and July 2025. Check the official notices before you go.

guia.kandersteg-bluemlisalphutte.torment.t: Summer thunderstorms. They are common in the afternoon. That's why you set off early.

guia.kandersteg-bluemlisalphutte.frio-y-.t: Cold and altitude. At 2,840 m it is cold even in summer, especially at night and at dawn.

guia.kandersteg-bluemlisalphutte.tiempo-.t: Weather. Check the forecast at MeteoSwiss and the hut's bulletin.

guia.kandersteg-bluemlisalphutte.julio-a.t: July to September: the hut is in full operation and the path is usually free of snow. It's the safest and busiest time.

guia.kandersteg-bluemlisalphutte.junio-y.t: June and October: the hut is open only part of the time and there may be snow or ice. Better to check before organising.

guia.kandersteg-bluemlisalphutte.resto-d.t: Rest of the year: it is not a hiking route; the winter room is for emergencies only.

guia.kandersteg-bluemlisalphutte.botas-d.t: Mountain boots with a good sole, already broken in (mandatory).

guia.kandersteg-bluemlisalphutte.ropa-po.t: Layered clothing, waterproof jacket, hat and gloves for the night and dawn.

guia.kandersteg-bluemlisalphutte.saco-sa.t: Sleeping-bag liner, headlamp, earplugs (shared dormitory) and minimal toiletries.

guia.kandersteg-bluemlisalphutte.agua-pa.t: Water for the climb and something to eat along the way. With Clas Tours, dinner, breakfast and 1 litre of hiking tea are included.

guia.kandersteg-bluemlisalphutte.bastone.t: Poles (highly recommended for the descent), sunscreen, sunglasses.

guia.kandersteg-bluemlisalphutte.traje-d.t: Swimwear and a small towel if you want to swim.

guia.kandersteg-bluemlisalphutte.tarjeta.t: Card or cash for drinks, and valid personal insurance.

guia.kandersteg-bluemlisalphutte.cuanto-.t: How long does the Griesalp – Blüemlisalphütte – Kandersteg crossing take?

guia.kandersteg-bluemlisalphutte.son-dos.t: It takes two days. The first climbs from Griesalp to the hut (about 4 to 4 h 30 of walking, +1,450 m). The second descends past the Oeschinensee to Kandersteg (about 3 to 4 h of walking, not counting breaks and the swim).

guia.kandersteg-bluemlisalphutte.es-una-.t: It is a demanding mountain route, T3 on the SAC scale according to BLS and Bergwelten. It has a steep section with chains towards the Hohtürli and a steep descent. Good fitness and no fear of heights are required.

guia.kandersteg-bluemlisalphutte.se-pued.t: Can it be done in a single day?

guia.kandersteg-bluemlisalphutte.si-hay-.t: Yes, some people do it in one go: about 16 km and close to 7 h 45 of walking according to Bergwelten, with +1,450 m of ascent. Sleeping at the hut lets you do it calmly and see the sunset and sunrise in the mountains.

guia.kandersteg-bluemlisalphutte.la-blue.t: The Blüemlisalphütte is staffed from mid-June to mid or late October, and in full operation from July to September. Outside those dates only the emergency room is open. Always book in advance.

guia.kandersteg-bluemlisalphutte.se-pued.t: Can you swim in the Oeschinensee?

guia.kandersteg-bluemlisalphutte.si-el-b.t: Yes, swimming is allowed, at your own risk. There are no changing rooms, showers or lifeguards. The water is cold, like a mountain lake, so go in slowly and only for a short time.

guia.kandersteg-bluemlisalphutte.como-vu.t: How do I get back to Kandersteg from the lake?

guia.kandersteg-bluemlisalphutte.puedes-.t: You can continue on foot along the Oeschibach stream to Kandersteg, or take the gondola from the lake for the last 400 m of descent. The gondola has seasonal timetables, so confirm them.

guia.kandersteg-bluemlisalphutte.que-ten.t: What do I need to bring to the hut?

guia.kandersteg-bluemlisalphutte.un-saco.t: A sleeping-bag liner (mandatory: the hut provides blankets but not sheets), card or cash for drinks, warm clothes, a headlamp and mountain footwear. Dinner and breakfast are included if you go with Clas Tours.
